      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.

      properties:

        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized into
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise country code '+61' is
            assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The
            result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The E.164 value is stored
            and returned, and duplicate telephones are detected by comparing it.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true on create, permits registering this owner even though another
            owner already has the same last name and address (they share a
            household). Optional; defaults to false. This flag is only a
            create-time hint and is not persisted.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:

          properties:

              type: integer

              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.

              example: Franklin, George
              readOnly: true
            initials:

              readOnly: true
            customerCode:

## Summary

I implemented `namesakeCount` on owner creation — the count of existing owners sharing the same first and last name (case-insensitively) *before* the new owner is persisted.

Changes:
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — computes and sets the count before saving, via a new `namesakeCount(firstName, lastName)` helper that reuses the existing `normalizeIdentity` (trim + collapse whitespace + lower-case) for the case-insensitive comparison against `findAllOwners()`, consistent with the household/telephone duplicate checks.
- **`Owner` model** — added a persisted `namesake_count` column with getter/setter (the value is read back on `GET /api/owners/{id}`).
- **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `namesakeCount` (int32, min 0) to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps it by name automatically.
- **schema.sql** (hsqldb/h2/postgres/mysql) — added the `namesake_count` column.

`mvn test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`. The test creates two owners with the same first/last name (different addresses to avoid the household 409) and asserts the second reports `namesakeCount = 1`.
